places.name: Haeundae Beach
places.description: Popular urban beach in Busan, an iconic seaside resort destination.
places.evidence: is an urban beach in Busan, South Korea, located in the eponymous Haeundae District.

places.name: Diamond Tower
places.description: A 120-metre tower offering panoramic views of Busan's harbor and cityscape.
places.evidence: is a 120-metre-high tower at Yongdusan Park, located in Jung District, Busan, South Korea.

places.name: Haedong Yonggungsa
places.description: A breathtaking seaside Buddhist temple cliffside, one of Busan's most iconic spiritual landmarks.
places.evidence: Haedong Yonggung Temple is a Buddhist temple in Gijang-gun, Busan, South Korea.

places.name: Gwangan Bridge
places.description: A striking suspension bridge connecting Haeundae and Suyeong districts with iconic night illumination.
places.evidence: is a suspension bridge located in Busan, South Korea. It connects Haeundae District to Suyeong District.

places.name: Beomeosa
places.description: One of Busan's most renowned temples, set on mountain slopes with serene forest surroundings.
places.evidence: Built on the slopes of the mountain Geumjeongsan, it is one of the country's best known temples.

places.name: Jagalchi Market
places.description: Korea's largest and most vibrant fish market with fresh seafood stalls and dining experiences.
places.evidence: is a fish market in Busan, South Korea. The market is located on the edge of Nampo Port (남포항), Busan. It is considered to be the largest fish market in South Korea.

places.name: Busan Cooperative Fish Market
places.description: Major cooperative fish market handling Korea's substantial catch with refrigerated facilities.
places.evidence: The Busan Cooperative Fish Market is the largest fish market in South Korea.

places.name: National Maritime Museum
places.description: Korea's third-largest museum focusing on maritime heritage and Busan's seafaring culture.
places.evidence: is a Korean maritime museum and the third largest museum in the South Korea.

places.name: United Nations Memorial Cemetery
places.description: The world's only UN cemetery with graves honoring Korean War servicemembers from multiple nations.
places.evidence: It contains 2,300 graves and is the only United Nations cemetery in the world.

places.name: Gaya Tumuli
places.description: A UNESCO World Heritage archaeological site comprising ancient tumuli complexes of the Gaya confederacy, spanning the 1st to late 6th century CE.
places.evidence: comprises seven tumuli complexes of the Gaya confederacy, from the 1st to the late 6th century CE

city_tips.title: Use a T-money Card for Transit
city_tips.content: Purchase a T-money or Cashbee card at convenience stores for seamless travel across metro, buses, and taxis with automatic discounts.
city_tips.evidence: Using the transportation card will save you money compared to paying cash.

city_tips.title: Busan is Very Safe to Explore
city_tips.content: Busan is as safe as most places in South Korea. Avoid areas around Busan Station late at night, and be cautious of occasional drunk patrons on late-night metro rides.
city_tips.evidence: Generally speaking Busan is as safe as most places in South Korea, which is to say very safe.

city_tips.title: Try Dong-nae Pajeon Locally
city_tips.content: Sample the Busan specialty of dong-nae pajeon, a seafood and green onion pancake that is affordable and widely available.
city_tips.evidence: Dong-nae pajeon (동래파전) is a seafood and green onion pancake, an affordable and popular Busan dish.

city_tips.title: Avoid Summer Peak Season
city_tips.content: Visit outside July-August when rates are high and beaches are crowded. Spring and fall offer pleasant weather and lower prices.
city_tips.evidence: Rates are very high during the summer peak season which varies by hotel but is roughly July to August).

places.name: Hallasan
places.description: The highest peak in South Korea at 1,947 metres, dominating Jeju Island with its shield volcano.
places.evidence: Hallasan (Korean: 한라산) is a shield volcano comprising much of Jeju Island in South Korea.

places.name: Seongsan Ilchulbong
places.description: A volcanic crater peak offering sunrise views with 182 metres elevation and visitor facilities.
places.evidence: It is 182 meters high and has a volcanic crater at the top.

places.name: Jeongbang Waterfall
places.description: A coastal waterfall dropping 23 metres directly into the sea, a unique tourist attraction.
places.evidence: Jeongbang Waterfall (Korean: 정방폭포) is a waterfall and popular tourist attraction located in Seogwipo, Jeju Province, South Korea.

places.name: Cheonjiyeon Waterfall
places.description: A tiered 22-metre waterfall famous for illumination at night, one of Jeju's scenic wonders.
places.evidence: Cheonjiyeon Waterfall (Korean: 천지연폭포) is a waterfall on Jeju Island, South Korea.

places.name: Cheonjeyeon Waterfalls
places.description: A three-tier waterfall ranking among Jeju's three most famous waterfalls.
places.evidence: The falls are a popular tourist attraction, and one of the three famous waterfalls of Jeju, alongside Cheonjiyeon Waterfall and Jeongbang Waterfall.

places.name: Manjanggul
places.description: The world's second-longest lava tube at 8.928 km, showcasing Jeju's volcanic geology.
places.evidence: At up to 23 metres (75 ft) wide, 30 metres (98 ft) high and 8.928 km long, it is the 12th-longest lava tube in the world and the second longest on Jeju Island.

places.name: Yakcheonsa
places.description: A Buddhist temple nestled in Seogwipo showcasing traditional Korean spiritual architecture.
places.evidence: Yakcheonsa is a Buddhist temple of the Jogye Order in Seogwipo, Jeju Province, South Korea.

places.name: Yeomiji Botanical Garden
places.description: A botanical garden in Jungmun Tourism Complex showcasing diverse plant collections.
places.evidence: Yeomiji Botanical Garden (Korean: 여미지식물관) is botanical garden in Jungmun Tourism Complex, Seogwipo, Jeju-do, South Korea.

places.name: Nexon Computer Museum
places.description: Computer museum dedicated to gaming and video game history, opened in 2013.
places.evidence: Opening on 27 July 2013, it is one of the first permanent museums in Korea that is dedicated to the history of computers and video games.

places.name: Wardah
places.description: A Yemeni restaurant in Jeju City, one of the few halal options on the island, run by a South Korean-Yemeni couple.
places.evidence: Wardah is a Yemeni restaurant in Jeju City, South Korea.
places.image_note: no Commons image for this place; city landmark image used

places.name: Jeju Dongmun Traditional Market
places.description: The largest and oldest extant permanent traditional market in Jeju, a covered market with local produce and street food stalls.
places.evidence: the largest and oldest extant permanent traditional market in Jeju

city_tips.title: Navigate by Bus with Google Maps
city_tips.content: Jeju's bus system is efficient but only in Korean. Use Google Maps for accurate navigation across the island's routes.
city_tips.evidence: Jeju City has an inner-city (shin-nae) bus system that is equally as efficient as it is poorly marked for tourists.

city_tips.title: Taste Local Hallabong Fruit
city_tips.content: Try Jeju's famous hallabong, a sweet honeyed orange cultivated since the 1990s and a registered geographical specialty.
city_tips.evidence: The most well known fruit is the hallabong.

city_tips.title: Traditional Fishing and Diving Villages
city_tips.content: Jeju's farm villages traditionally centered on farming alongside fishing and diving fishery in coastal fishing villages.
city_tips.evidence: Life in the farm villages was centered on farming, as it did around fishing or diving fishery in fishing villages

city_tips.title: Visit Spring or Fall for Weather
city_tips.content: Jeju winters are quite warm - Chinese cabbages are even left growing in the fields through the season.
city_tips.evidence: It is quite warm during the winter and Chinese cabbages are left in the field.

places.name: National Palace Museum
places.description: A national museum with collections of Chinese treasures and cultural relics, founded in Beijing in 1925.
places.evidence: Founded in Beijing in 1925, the museum was re-established in Shilin, Taipei, in 1965, later expanded with a southern branch in Taibao, Chiayi, in 2015.

places.name: Chiang Kai-shek Memorial Hall
places.description: A national monument and tourist attraction honoring former President Chiang Kai-shek with classical architecture.
places.evidence: In recent years, the site has also incorporated remembrance of Taiwan’s martial law period (1949–1987).

places.name: Taipei Grand Mosque

places.name: Taipei Zoo
places.description: Taiwan's most famous zoo, a large public zoological garden in Wenshan District that is also a leader in conservation and research.

places.name: Songshan Market

places.name: Shilin Night Market
places.description: Often called the largest and most famous night market in Taiwan, packed with street-food stalls in Shilin District.
places.evidence: Shilin Night Market is a night market in Shilin District, Taipei, Taiwan, often considered to be the largest and most famous night market in Taiwan.

places.name: Bangka Lungshan Temple
places.description: A Taiwanese folk temple in Wanhua District built in 1738 by Fujian settlers, honoring Guanyin alongside Chinese folk deities like Mazu and Guan Yu.
places.evidence: Bangka Lungshan Temple is a Taiwanese folk temple in Wanhua District, Taipei, Taiwan.

city_tips.title: Use EasyCard for Transit Discounts
city_tips.content: Purchase an EasyCard for automatic discounts on metro and buses. Transfers between modes within an hour get discounted fares.
city_tips.evidence: Taipei City has a very clean, efficient and safe Mass Rapid Transit system known most commonly as the MRT, but also called Metro Taipei ().

city_tips.title: Taipei is Extremely Safe
city_tips.content: Violent crime is rare. Stay alert in crowded areas for pickpockets and avoid isolated areas late at night.
city_tips.evidence: Taipei is one of the safest cities you will ever visit, and violent crime is extremely rare.

city_tips.title: Explore Night Markets for Street Food
city_tips.content: Visit famous night markets like Shilin or Raohe for authentic Taiwanese street snacks, oyster omelets, and stinky tofu.
city_tips.evidence: The most famous one in Taipei is the Shilin Night Market

city_tips.title: Learn Basic Mandarin or Use Translation Apps
city_tips.content: Most taxi drivers speak minimal English. Have destinations written in Chinese or use translation apps for easier navigation.
city_tips.evidence: Stations are clearly identified in English as well as Chinese.
